title: Merge keeps worktree by default; queue worktree-cleanup entry
action: Flip merge cleanup default to KEEP: teardown only when --cleanup passed or worktree_cleanup_on_merge=true explicit in config; --no-cleanup stays explicit keep and wins over config true. Re-arm --cleanup (no-op today, worktree/mod.rs:9-11; resolver resolve_cleanup_on_merge handlers.rs:426). On keep path after green merge: add kind worktree-cleanup to KINDS in deferred_queue.rs and enqueue one entry — feature = creation-identity slug (fallback worktree id), files=[worktree_root], reason names worktree id, branch, merge sha, and 'bee worktree prune' as the remove command. Keep cleanup_suggested_command in output. Registration (grants+workspace record) stays. Sweep KINDS consumers (status_full, session_preamble/store.rs, chain_nudge.rs) for exhaustive-match breaks. Flip existing default-cleanup test assertions; add: default merge keeps and enqueues exactly one entry; --cleanup tears down and enqueues nothing.

truths: Default green merge keeps worktree, branch, registration
Exactly one worktree-cleanup entry appended on keep path

deviations: Wiring the keep-path enqueue required touching phases.rs (merge_finish's post-commit success arm), not in the cell's declared files — the actual git-commit success path lives there, not in merge.rs; reserved it before commit after confirming no conflict.
trace.inline_reason: Dispatched as execution worker wkm-w1 by the orchestrator for cell wkm-1 (per dispatch prompt), but state.json workers[] has no registration entry for this worker/cell — registering it is orchestrator-side (bee state worker add), not something this worker performs; proceeding per the documented --inline-reason path rather than guessing at control-plane state.
